My cat needed to be hospitalized at the Guarani unit, where he initially received emergency care.
After being evaluated and medicated, we were informed that the clinic would contact us by phone between 11 am and 1 pm to provide information and updates on his condition.
We scheduled the appointment for 9 pm because we work far away and the clinic is close to home. We arrived right on time, eager to be able to visit, but to our surprise, we had to wait for over an hour to see our cat because we weren't informed that even though we had scheduled an appointment, whoever arrived first would be seen (it was scheduled).

However, when we asked for the invoice, we saw that the amount charged for hospitalization didn't match the total on the invoice, and the person who was assisting us said that at the time of admission, an additional X-ray was requested but not performed (we're talking about an expensive exam, $600+), for which we paid for everything, and the credit refund was only $100. In other words, we feel wronged because they took advantage of our emotional vulnerability and desperation to charge the amount that was charged, and we still have to go through all this time to visit our kitten.
If we hadn't asked for the invoice and noticed the difference between the amount paid and the amount declared, they would NEVER have brought the issue to our attention.
He was hospitalized from July 26th to 28th, and today, August 13th, we have to contact the institution almost every day because, to this day, they have not refunded the difference paid, which makes a difference to us.
The establishment did not act transparently with us; in fact, I do not recommend them!
Extremely disappointed with the clinic.

The day before, we spent around R$ 1,000.00 at Vet Popular on consultations, exams, and medication for our pet, Keka. The veterinarian herself asked us to return as soon as possible once the results were available.

We followed the instructions and arrived at the clinic yesterday, around 9:40 PM, with the exams in hand. The reception area was empty; there was no one ahead of us. Even so, we were ignored. We waited for ONE HOUR—me, my wife, and our 2-year-old son, in addition to Keka.

We asked at reception after 15 minutes of waiting, then after 30 minutes, and the employees just said they "would see" and disappeared without giving any answers. Only after an hour, when I needed to be firmer and demand a position, did the attendant go to speak with the veterinarian and return saying that the service would take a while.
The biggest absurdity was the omission. If they had been honest from the beginning, we would have come back another day. Instead, they left us tired with a 2-year-old child waiting in the lobby. It was clear that, because it was a "return" (where the money had already been deposited the day before), Keka's case lost priority. A gigantic lack of respect and empathy. I do not recommend!

Terrible place. I took my dog, who was 100% fine, on Monday, and after returning from a walk about 2 hours later, he became dizzy and fell. We rushed him to the 24-hour public clinic where he was medicated and given medicine to take home. The next day there was no improvement, so we took him to the Sapopemba clinic.
There, we initially spent $1900 because they said the dog needed two X-rays, tests, and hospitalization.
The dog was healthy; it was after the walk that we suspected a bite from a venomous animal and informed them.
They said they looked for a bite on the body and didn't find one. How can someone search the body of a 4-year-old German Shepherd full of fur?
The next day when we returned, they requested more albumin tests, an ultrasound, and more X-rays, another expense of $1100. And they informed us that the dog had liver cancer pressing on his stomach, that he couldn't eat because he would vomit.
So, I'm talking about a 4-year-old dog who, just two days before, would eat the house if you let him and never vomited. He got sick after a 2-hour walk where he went into the bushes.
With terminal cancer?
He had tests done, but the results haven't come back yet. I sent the ones I had to another veterinarian who, without examining the dog, said he might have been bitten by an animal, or even caught a rat, etc., and that he would transfer the dog the next day.
Around 10 PM, they called me informing me that the dog had cardiac arrest and died, and they even charged $275 to remove the body.
Then the question is, how can a healthy, active, gluttonous, 100% 4-year-old dog develop terminal cancer in 24 hours, undergo a bunch of tests, and then go into cardiac arrest?
Was that really it? Or were they just sucking our money and treating him incorrectly to keep him there, since the test results weren't given to us to take to another place for evaluation? It's not about the money, but so they don't have to go through what my family and I are going through.

Everything is overpriced.

They even charge extra for medications during hospitalization or supplements.

My experience at this clinic had some good service, but one instance in particular was extremely negative.
The veterinarian Pamela provided this service.

My dog ​​was pregnant and close to giving birth. We took her in for exams to check her condition. During the consultation, the veterinarian didn't know how to use the ultrasound machine, and even said she would press all the buttons until she got it right. We couldn't see the puppy's heartbeat in either the ultrasound image or the sound waves, I believe partly because the veterinarian didn't know how to use the machine. This created a lot of insecurity with the professional. Despite this, she informed us that the puppy was alive and that its head was turned to come out.

A day later, she started giving birth to the already deceased and decomposing puppy, which came out with its hind legs first.

If the veterinarian doesn't know how to use the machine, just call someone who does. My impression is that she made up that information because the exams were inconclusive.

Congratulations to the company that insisted on contacting me for a month to try to understand what went wrong, apologize, and find out what to improve in future customer service interactions.
